title: Creative Video Editor & Social Media Growth Specialist
description:
MCAT Simplified is hiring a full-time Creative Video Editor & Content Growth Specialist to help grow our YouTube, Instagram, and TikTok presence.



We help aspiring doctors prepare for the MCAT. We’re looking for a versatile, highly creative editor who can turn newly filmed footage into compelling videos, develop original content ideas, repurpose existing recordings, and use performance data to guide our growth.



You should understand how to make people stop scrolling, feel something, keep watching, and connect with our brand. Strong editing skills, storytelling, creative initiative, and an understanding of social media strategy are essential.



WHAT YOU’LL DO



• Turn our newly filmed footage into polished, engaging videos with a clear story, strong hook, and satisfying payoff.

• Use captions, our available B-roll, music, sound design, graphics, and thoughtful pacing to strengthen each video.

• Create emotionally compelling content that connects with students’ ambitions, frustrations, challenges, and successes while staying authentic to our brand.

• Work across different formats, including educational videos, talking-head content, motivational storytelling, student success stories, promotional videos, and longer YouTube videos.

• Contribute ideas before filming: suggest concepts, hooks, scripts, talking points, and additional shots that would improve the finished video.

• Identify valuable moments in existing lessons and recordings, then turn them into engaging standalone clips.

• Adapt content for Instagram Reels, TikTok, YouTube Shorts, and long-form YouTube rather than using the same approach for every platform.

• Develop compelling title and thumbnail concepts, recurring content series, and new creative approaches.

• Help maintain a consistent flow of high-quality content through organized planning, editing, and delivery.

• Learn our brand voice, products, and audience so your creative decisions support our broader business goals.



PERFORMANCE ANALYSIS & WEEKLY MEETINGS



You will also help us understand what is working and how to improve.



• Review video performance, including views, retention, watch time, click-through rates, shares, saves, and follower growth, where available.

• Come to each weekly team meeting prepared with a concise report showing what was published, how it performed, and what we learned.

• Analyze strong and weak performers, identifying patterns in topics, hooks, storytelling, pacing, and presentation.

• Bring specific recommendations, fresh content ideas, and experiments for the following week.

• Track the results of those experiments and apply what you learn to future videos.



WHO WE’RE LOOKING FOR



• A versatile portfolio showing original video production from supplied footage, short-form editing, and strong storytelling.

• Excellent creative judgment: you know when to add visual interest, build emotion, simplify an edit, or let a moment breathe.

• Strong skills in captions, B-roll selection, audio editing, music selection, color correction, and basic motion graphics.

• An understanding of audience psychology, platform-specific content, and social media growth.

• The ability to take raw footage and a general direction and independently develop a strong finished video.

• Initiative in proposing ideas and improving our content—not waiting for detailed instructions on every edit.

• Comfort analyzing performance data and presenting useful recommendations.

• Strong English comprehension and attention to accuracy when editing educational content.

• Reliable communication, organization, and the ability to meet deadlines.

• Proficiency in Premiere Pro, DaVinci Resolve, Final Cut Pro, CapCut, or comparable software, with reliable equipment and internet access.



Experience helping a brand grow through content is a strong plus. Medical or MCAT knowledge is not required, but curiosity and a willingness to understand our audience are essential.



ROLE DETAILS



• Full-time, remote

• 40 hours per week

• $5 USD per hour

• Weekly team meetings



HOW TO APPLY



Use “MCAT Creative Editor” as your application subject and include:



A brief introduction explaining why you fit this combination of editing, creativity, and content strategy.

Links to 3–5 videos demonstrating your range. Include at least one video you built from raw footage and explain your contribution.

Any measurable content performance or growth results, including the timeframe and your role.

Two original video ideas for MCAT Simplified, with a suggested hook and editing approach for each.

A brief example of how you used analytics to improve content.

Your editing software, availability, time zone, and confirmation that the hours and pay work for you.



We want someone who takes ownership of their creative work and is excited to help us build content that resonates with students and grows our brand.

title: China sourcing and procurement specialist
description:
China Sourcing & Procurement Specialist



Products: SPC/LVP Flooring & RTA Kitchen Cabinets



We are a U.S.-based construction and remodeling company looking for an experienced China Sourcing & Procurement Specialist to help us source building materials directly from manufacturers in China.



This is NOT a general virtual assistant position.



We are specifically looking for someone who has experience sourcing products from Chinese manufacturers using 1688, Alibaba, direct factory contacts, and other Chinese sourcing channels.



Our initial focus is:



1. SPC/LVP Flooring

2. RTA Kitchen Cabinets



If the relationship is successful, additional construction products may be added later.



YOUR RESPONSIBILITIES



You will be responsible for researching, locating, verifying, negotiating with, and comparing Chinese manufacturers.



We do NOT simply want the cheapest supplier.



We want the best combination of price, quality, reliability, certifications, shipping cost, and manufacturer credibility.



You will:



• Locate actual manufacturers/factories rather than unnecessary middlemen or trading companies.



• Search Alibaba, 1688, Chinese manufacturer directories, and other appropriate sourcing channels.



• Communicate directly with factories.



• Determine whether each supplier is a manufacturer, trading company, or sourcing agent.



• Obtain and negotiate factory pricing.



• Negotiate MOQ requirements.



• Request samples.



• Obtain product specifications and technical documentation.



• Obtain available U.S.-market certifications and testing reports.



• Compare several manufacturers rather than recommending the first supplier you find.



• Investigate the supplier's history, factory capabilities, production capacity, export experience, and reputation.



• Determine production lead times.



• Obtain packaging specifications, carton/pallet dimensions and weights.



• Determine how much product fits into 20-foot and 40-foot containers when applicable.



• Obtain FOB and other relevant shipping quotations.



• Help coordinate freight-forwarding quotations to New Jersey, USA.



• Help calculate the approximate landed cost in New Jersey, not simply the factory purchase price.



• Assist with quality-control inspections before final payment/shipment.



• Maintain organized records of suppliers, quotations, samples, specifications and communications.



FLOORING SOURCING



We are particularly interested in quality SPC/LVP waterproof flooring suitable for residential and light-commercial construction.



You should be able to compare manufacturers based on items including:



• SPC construction

• Overall plank thickness

• Wear-layer thickness

• Attached underlayment/padding

• Click-lock system

• Residential/commercial warranty

• Scratch and wear resistance

• Waterproof performance

• Available colors/designs

• Packaging

• Square footage per carton

• Pallet quantities

• Container quantities

• Certifications/testing

• MOQ

• Factory price per square meter/square foot

• FOB price

• Production time

• Sample availability



We will determine final specifications after reviewing factory options.



CABINET SOURCING



We are primarily interested in RTA (Ready-to-Assemble) kitchen cabinets because shipping efficiency is important.



We want manufacturers capable of producing cabinet lines appropriate for the U.S. remodeling market.



You should compare:



• Cabinet-box construction

• Plywood vs. particleboard/MDF components

• Box thickness

• Door construction

• Painted and stained finishes

• Shaker-style availability

• Soft-close hinges

• Soft-close drawer slides

• Drawer-box construction

• Hardware quality

• Standard U.S. cabinet dimensions

• Available cabinet sizes/SKUs

• Matching panels, fillers, moldings and accessories

• Packaging quality

• Replacement-part policy

• Warranty

• MOQ

• Sample/demo cabinet availability

• Container capacity

• Factory pricing

• FOB pricing

• Production lead time



WHAT WE DO NOT WANT



We do not want someone who simply searches Alibaba, copies several links and sends them to us.



We can do that ourselves.



Your value is in finding the factory behind the product, communicating with the manufacturer, negotiating, verifying information, identifying problems, and determining the true cost of getting the product to us in the United States.



We expect you to question suppliers and verify claims rather than simply accepting what a salesperson tells you.



EXPERIENCE WE ARE LOOKING FOR



Strong candidates should have experience with several of the following:



• China product sourcing

• 1688 sourcing

• Alibaba sourcing

• Factory verification

• Supplier negotiation

• Procurement

• Import/export

• Quality control

• Freight forwarding

• Container shipping

• U.S. imports

• Building materials

• Flooring

• Kitchen cabinets



Mandarin/Chinese-language ability is a major advantage.



Experience specifically sourcing construction materials, SPC flooring, LVP flooring, cabinetry, furniture or building products is highly preferred.



PAID/TRIAL SOURCING ASSIGNMENT



Before selecting someone for ongoing work, qualified applicants may be given a sourcing assignment.



You may be asked to identify:



3 legitimate SPC/LVP flooring manufacturers



and



3 legitimate RTA kitchen-cabinet manufacturers.



For each manufacturer, we want a comparison showing:



1. Factory/company name

2. Factory location

3. Manufacturer vs. trading company

4. Years in business

5. Main products

6. Export experience to the United States

7. Product specifications

8. Certifications/testing documentation

9. MOQ

10. Sample cost

11. Unit/factory price

12. FOB price

13. Production lead time

14. Packaging information

15. Container capacity

16. Payment terms

17. Quality-control options

18. Freight estimate to New Jersey, if available

19. Approximate landed cost

20. Your assessment of the supplier and any concerns/red flags



Simply submitting Alibaba links will NOT qualify as completing the assignment.



HOW TO APPLY



Please begin your application with the words:



“FACTORY DIRECT”



This lets us know you read the entire posting.



Then answer these questions:



1. How many years have you worked in China sourcing/procurement?



2. Do you personally use 1688?



3. Can you communicate with suppliers in Mandarin/Chinese?



4. Have you sourced products for U.S. companies before?



5. Have you sourced flooring, cabinets, furniture, construction materials or similar products?



6. How do you determine whether a supplier is an actual manufacturer rather than a trading company?



7. How do you verify a Chinese factory before a buyer sends a substantial deposit?



8. What methods do you use to negotiate better pricing and MOQ?



9. Have you coordinated third-party factory inspections?



10. Have you worked with freight forwarders and container shipments to the United States?



11. Provide an example of a sourcing project you completed and explain how you reduced the buyer's cost or prevented a sourcing problem.



12. What is your hourly or project-based rate?



IMPORTANT



We are looking for a long-term sourcing relationship, but we will start small.



Our goal is to establish reliable direct relationships with manufacturers that can supply our construction company at pricing that makes financial sense after product cost + freight + duties/tariffs + customs/brokerage + inspections + inland transportation + all other import expenses.



We care about the number that matters:



THE FINAL LANDED COST IN NEW JERSEY.



If you are experienced in finding legitimate Chinese manufacturers, negotiating factory-direct pricing and protecting buyers from sourcing mistakes, we would like to hear from you.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

- Generate short AI video content, including satisfying recipe and product videos — ingredients coming together, product reveals, close-up food/product shots

- Use tools like Grok Imagine and Gemini Nano Banana (and stay current on new tools as they emerge) to produce imagery that reads as authentic photography/videography, not AI-generated

- Maintain visual and brand consistency across a fast-moving content calendar

- Iterate quickly based on ad performance data — what's working, what's not, and why

- Continuously push creative quality and volume without sacrificing either



WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR



- Proven ability to produce AI statics that look realistic — this is non-negotiable. Our audience notices and dislikes anything that reads as "AI slop"

- Hands-on experience with AI image/video tools like Grok Imagine and Gemini Nano Banana (and openness to picking up new tools as they emerge)

- Comfort producing high volume without quality drop-off

- Strong eye for food, product, and lifestyle photography aesthetics

- Self-direction — you should be able to take loose creative direction and run

- Bonus: experience with Meta Ads creative testing and understanding what visual patterns drive performance



COMPENSATION



This is an hourly + performance role.



- Base pay: $5–$10/hour, depending on experience level

- Performance bonuses: on top of base, for high-performing ads (based on Meta Ads metrics) and for high production volume



We want this to reward output and results, not just time logged — the bonus structure is where the real upside is for the right person.



HIRING PROCESS



1. Application — respond to this posting with answers to the questions below

2. Trial task — if selected based on your application, you'll be sent a paid/unpaid trial task

3. Interview — if you do well on the trial task, you'll interview directly with the founder

4. Hire — offer extended from there, starting part-time with a path to full-time



HOW TO APPLY



This posting will get a lot of applicants, so we're using the application itself as a first filter. Please answer the following in your application. Short, direct answers are fine — we care more about substance than polish here.



1. Why are you passionate about health and wellness?

2. How have you personally committed to health and wellness in your own life?

3. What accomplishments are you proud of — creative, professional, or personal?

4. How much experience do you have with graphic design and/or AI-generated design specifically?

5. What AI tools do you currently have access to (paid subscriptions, free tiers, etc.)?

6. What's your experience with each of the following: Grok Imagine, Gemini Nano Banana, and any other AI image/video tools you use? Be specific about what you've made with each.

7. Roughly how much output have you produced with these specific tools (volume, timeframe, context)?

8. What do you think is your single greatest strength for this role? Are you fastest at high-quality output? Most creative/out-of-the-box? Most consistent at hitting photorealism? Tell us what makes you the right fit, specifically.

9. Tell us about your current work setup: Do you have any clients you're currently working for? Do you have capacity to ramp to full-time if this goes well? Is your setup comfortable for working remotely? What's your Wi-Fi speed? Do you have a workspace you can use daily for a full-time workload?

10. Please link a portfolio or samples of past work (AI-generated or otherwise).



One more thing: to confirm you've read this entire posting, end your application with the word "homemade" as the very last word of your submission.

title: Telecommunications / Electrical Design Engineer – AutoCAD & Technical Work Packages (Part-Time)
description:
Engineering Project Desk is seeking a part-time remote Telecommunications / Electrical Design Engineer who can independently investigate engineering problems, evaluate equipment upgrades, propose defensible solutions, and produce clear drawings and technical work packages for review.



HOURS AND COMPENSATION

Approximately 15–20 hours per week. Initial target rate: USD $6–$8/hour, based on demonstrated capability. Higher compensation may be considered after proven performance. Remote work with agreed deadlines and scheduled coordination.



WHAT YOU WILL DO

• Analyze existing conditions and integration requirements using sanitized drawings, technical notes, and public equipment manuals.

• Research and compare technical solutions; document calculations, assumptions, alternatives, risks, and recommendations.

• Develop AutoCAD drawings, wiring/interconnection diagrams, equipment layouts, revisions, and PDF deliverables.

• Support telecommunications, radio communications, IP networking, audio/control interfaces, and DC power integration.

• Prepare bills of materials and technical work packages covering scope, removal/installation, wiring, configuration requirements, testing, acceptance criteria, and contingency steps.

• Cite technical sources by document title, revision, and page/section; reconcile drawings, BOMs, and written instructions.

• Flag missing information as TBD / ENGINEER TO CONFIRM. Never invent pinouts, ratings, settings, or design requirements.

• Maintain organized Google Drive project files, revision records, time reports, and QA/QC responses.



REQUIRED CAPABILITIES

• Electrical, electronics, telecommunications, or closely related engineering education and relevant practical design experience.

• Independent technical problem-solving and systems integration experience.

• Strong AutoCAD capability and ability to read schematics, manuals, and specifications.

• Clear written English and well-organized engineering documentation.

• Ability to explain and defend your own calculations, design choices, and deliverables during live discussion.

• Reliable remote availability for approximately 15–20 hours/week.



SANITIZED PROJECT WORKFLOW

Work uses fictional or sanitized project information and approved references. Follow confidentiality, access, and revision-control requirements. Do not upload project material to unapproved services or subcontract the work. Deliverables are drafts subject to owner technical review and approval.



SELECTION PROCESS

1. Initial application and portfolio screening.

2. First technical engineering test using a fictional/sanitized problem.

3. Additional progressively harder technical tests for applicants who advance, to assess engineering judgment, integration, calculations, drawings, and work-package quality.

4. Live technical verification/interview: explain your submission and respond to a changed requirement.

5. Paid finalist trial before a hiring decision, with scope, rate, and time limit agreed in advance.

Only shortlisted applicants advance. Assessment instructions and time expectations will be provided at each stage. Submit your own work and disclose any tools or assistance used; you must understand and explain every technical conclusion.



PROBATION AFTER HIRE

The probation period is 3 months / 90 days, with formal review gates at Day 30, Day 60, and Day 90. Reviews assess technical accuracy, independent problem-solving, research/source quality, drawing and work-package quality, communication, productivity, and confidentiality. The final probation decision is at Day 90. Access remains limited to approved sanitized materials throughout.



HOW TO APPLY

Apply directly through this job posting on OnlineJobs.ph using the website’s application system. Use the subject: Telecom Engineer – [Your Name]. Submit your application and communicate through OnlineJobs.ph. Include:

1. Resume and relevant engineering education/experience.

2. One example of a technical problem or equipment upgrade you solved independently: the problem, your reasoning, and result.

3. Your AutoCAD experience and examples of drawings/work packages you personally produced, with all client/employer and sensitive information removed. Share only material you are authorized to share.

4. Experience with telecommunications, electrical/control interfaces, IP networks, and DC power systems.

5. Expected hourly rate, weekly availability, time zone, and earliest start date.

6. Confirmation that you are willing to complete the staged assessments, live verification, paid finalist trial, and 3 months / 90 days probation with formal 30/60/90-day review gates.



Please do not send confidential documents from current or former employers.

title: WordPress / Elementor Expert Needed to Set Up Blog Post Templates
description:
I’m looking for an experienced WordPress/Elementor freelancer to clean up and properly configure the blog post templates on an existing website.



This is a relatively small, defined project. I am not looking for someone to write content or format individual blog posts on an ongoing basis.



The goal is to create a system where I can write or paste articles into the standard WordPress block editor, add images, headings and links, and have the finished article automatically display correctly using the Elementor template.



I do not want to use Elementor to build or format each individual blog post.



What I Need



I currently have three blog/post templates that need to be created or properly configured in Elementor.



I will provide examples of the look and layout I want.



The templates should control the overall design while allowing the actual article content to be created entirely through the standard WordPress post editor.



Each template should include the appropriate Elementor Post Content widget and dynamically pull in the post title, featured image, article content and other applicable post information.



Article Formatting



This is particularly important.



I publish long-form articles, generally between 1,000 and 2,500 words.



I need consistent formatting for:



* Paragraphs

* H2 headings

* H3 headings

* Bulleted and numbered lists

* Hyperlinks

* Bold and italic text

* Blockquotes, if used

* Images inserted within the article

* Image captions, if used



Paragraph and heading spacing should be controlled by the template/CSS rather than by manually adding blank lines to every article.



For example, paragraphs should automatically have appropriate spacing beneath them. H2 and H3 headings should automatically have appropriate spacing above and below them.



If I change a paragraph to an H2 in the WordPress editor, it should not affect or reset the formatting elsewhere in the article.



Images Within Articles



I frequently use images throughout an article in addition to the featured image.



A typical 1,200-word article may have a featured image plus two images within the article.



A 2,000-word article may have a featured image plus three or four images within the article.



I need to be able to insert these images directly into the WordPress block editor wherever I want them.



The template should automatically display these images properly, including consistent width, spacing and responsive behavior.



Mobile and Tablet



All three templates need to be tested and formatted properly for:



* Desktop

* Tablet

* Mobile



Typography, margins, images and spacing should remain clean and readable at each size.



The Most Important Deliverable



When the project is finished, I should be able to:



1. Go to WordPress → Posts → Add New

2. Enter the post title

3. Paste an article into the WordPress block editor

4. Assign H2 and H3 headings

5. Insert images wherever I want them

6. Add hyperlinks and internal links

7. Select the appropriate featured image

8. Publish



I should NOT need to click "Edit with Elementor" or manually adjust paragraph spacing, headings or formatting for each new article.**



That is the main purpose of this project.



Testing Before Completion



Before considering the project complete, I want each applicable template tested with an actual sample article.



The test article should include:



* Approximately 1,500+ words

* Multiple paragraphs

* Several H2 headings

* At least one H3 heading

* A bulleted list

* Internal/external hyperlinks

* Featured image

* At least three images inserted throughout the article



I want to see that the post displays correctly on desktop, tablet and mobile without manually formatting the individual post in Elementor.



Existing Website



This is an existing WordPress/Elementor website. I am not looking for a website redesign.



Please do not make unrelated changes to the website, theme, plugins, global styling or existing pages without discussing them with me first.



Please work carefully so existing pages and posts are not affected unexpectedly.



If CSS or global settings need to be changed, please explain what you intend to change before making changes that could affect other parts of the website.



Documentation / Handoff



At completion, I would like a short walkthrough, either live or a brief screen recording, showing me:



* How to create a new post

* How to select/use the appropriate template

* How to add H2/H3 headings

* How to insert article images

* How to add internal links

* How to change the featured image

* Anything I should avoid doing that could break the formatting



The system should be simple enough that I can publish future articles myself.



Who I'm Looking For



Please apply only if you have strong experience with:



* WordPress

* Elementor / Elementor Pro

* Elementor Theme Builder

* Single Post templates

* WordPress Gutenberg/block editor

* Dynamic post content

* Responsive design

* CSS and typography/spacing



Experience specifically setting up Elementor templates for content-heavy blogs is preferred.



When Applying



Please include:



1. A brief description of your experience with Elementor Single Post templates.

2. An example of a blog or content-heavy WordPress site you have set up.

3. Confirmation that you understand the goal is for me to create future articles in the WordPress block editor without using Elementor to format each individual article.

4. Your estimated turnaround time.

5. Your fixed-price quote for completing the project.



Please start your application with the words Block Editor so I know you read the full description.

title: Full-Time Social Media & Brand Manager (Remote)
description:
Position Overview

We are seeking an experienced, creative, and highly organized Social Media & Brand Manager to build and manage the online presence of a growing luxury residential construction and real estate brand. This is more than a posting role. You will be responsible for brand strategy, content planning, storytelling, social media management, creative coordination, and eventually buyer/Realtor lead generation.

The initial focus will be documenting the brand's first residential project from Day Zero through completion, with the marketing strategy gradually shifting toward property promotion and sales as the project nears completion.



Key Responsibilities

● Develop weekly and monthly social media strategies and content calendars.

● Manage Instagram, TikTok, YouTube Shorts, and Stories.

● Schedule and publish high-quality content consistently.

● Write engaging, professional, and premium captions and copy.

● Organize project photos, videos, renders, graphics, and marketing assets.

● Coordinate with video editors, graphic designers, photographers, and local content creators.

● Review raw footage and identify opportunities for Reels, TikToks, Shorts, Stories, and carousels.

● Communicate with management about what needs to be filmed and when.

● Document major construction milestones from demolition to completion.

● Maintain a consistent luxury brand identity, tone, and visual style.

● Research relevant trends while maintaining a sophisticated brand image.

● Monitor analytics, engagement, website traffic, inquiries, and leads.

● Maintain an organized database of potential buyers and Realtors.

● Support future property launches, private previews, floor plan releases, and sales campaigns.

● Prepare a concise weekly report covering content, upcoming filming needs, performance, and leads.



Content Pillars

Content should be built around:

1. The Build Demolition, excavation, foundation, framing, rough-ins, insulation, drywall, cabinetry, finishes, landscaping, and completion.

2. Construction Education Waterproofing, framing, insulation, HVAC, plumbing, electrical, roofing, windows, structural details, and other behind-the-wall work.

3. Design Kitchens, bathrooms, flooring, cabinets, lighting, fixtures, materials, architectural details, floor plans, and interior/exterior design.

4. Transformation Show the journey from Existing House → Demolition → Construction → Interior → Finished Home.

5. Brand Company philosophy, construction decisions, quality standards, founder/project insights, and behind-the-scenes stories.



Content Targets

Approximately:

● 2 high-quality Reels per week

● 1 carousel/photo post per week

● 3–7 Stories per week

● TikTok and YouTube Shorts adaptations

Quality is more important than quantity.



Capture everything. Post strategically.



Project Documentation

The manager will coordinate content capture for major milestones including:

● Day Zero / Existing Property

● Demolition

● Excavation & Foundation

● Framing

● Rough-ins / Mechanical

● Insulation & Drywall

● Cabinetry & Millwork

● Interior Finishes

● Exterior & Landscaping

● Near Completion

● Final Professional Photography & Video



All footage must be properly organized so it can be reused for future marketing and portfolio content.

Qualifications



● 3–5+ years of experience in social media, content management, digital marketing, or a related role.

● Proven experience managing social media for a business, brand, real estate, construction, architecture, design, or other visual industry.

● Strong knowledge of Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube Shorts.

● Excellent written and verbal English.

● Strong copywriting, storytelling, and content strategy skills.

● Excellent organization and time management.

● Experience coordinating with creative professionals.

● Ability to analyze social media performance.

● Able to work independently and meet deadlines.

● Strong understanding of professional and luxury brand presentation.

● Reliable high-speed internet and professional remote-work setup.



Preferred

● Experience with luxury real estate, construction, architecture, interior design, or property development.

● Strong understanding of premium visual branding.

● Canva, Adobe, CapCut, or similar tools.

● Meta Business Suite and social analytics.

● Basic video editing and graphic design.

● Google Drive/content asset management.

● Website/WordPress/Webflow experience.

● Lead generation and digital marketing experience.

● Strong visual judgment and short-form storytelling skills.



Important: This is NOT a basic social media posting position.

We are looking for someone who thinks like a Brand Manager and Content Strategist.



You should be able to answer:

What should we film?

Why should we film it?

How should we present it?

When should we publish it?

What story does it tell?

How does it strengthen the brand?

How can it eventually generate buyers and Realtor relationships?



You are expected to proactively identify content opportunities and communicate filming requirements to management.



Growth Opportunities

High-performing candidates may have opportunities to:

● Lead the overall digital brand strategy.

● Manage social media for future projects.

● Lead creative and marketing team members.

● Manage photographers and content creators.

● Participate in property launches and sales campaigns.

● Advance into Senior Brand/Marketing Management.

● Receive performance-based incentives as the company grows.



Why Join?

● 100% remote position.

● Help build a luxury residential brand from the ground up.

● Document a complete residential project from Day Zero to finished home.

● Significant creative and strategic ownership.

● Opportunity to build a long-term portfolio and marketing system.

● Growth opportunities as the company expands into future projects.



How to Apply

Please send to: 

● Updated Resume/CV

● Links to 3–5 social media accounts or brands you have managed

● Portfolio or examples of your work

● 2–3 minute audio introduction

● Brief summary of your content strategy and creative coordination experience

● Brief explanation of why you are interested in the role



Application Questions

1. If demolition begins Monday, what content would you capture before, during, and after?

2. What would your first 30 days of content look like for a new luxury residential brand?

3. How would you turn a normal construction update into an engaging Reel?

4. What luxury brands have excellent social media branding, and why?

5. How would you balance brand building with future buyer and Realtor lead generation?



Subject: Social Media & Brand Manager Application – Your Full Name



Note: Only shortlisted applicants will be contacted.

title: AI Animation & Story Video Creator
description:
# AI Animation & Story Video Creator



We are looking for a part-time **AI Video Creator** focused specifically on **story-driven, character-based AI videos**.



We create videos with recurring characters, multiple scenes, dialogue, comedy, cinematic sequences, and animated or stylized visual worlds. Think short AI films and animated social content rather than traditional UGC advertisements.



## What You'll Do



* Turn scripts and storyboards into AI-generated video scenes

* Create consistent characters across multiple shots and environments

* Generate reference images and animate them into scenes

* Create animated and stylized videos inspired by formats such as cartoons, video games, 3D animation, and cinematic films

* Control character actions, dialogue, camera angles, expressions, and scene blocking

* Regenerate and troubleshoot scenes when the AI makes mistakes

* Maintain consistency in faces, clothing, props, locations, and visual style

* Stitch generated scenes together and perform basic editing

* Help improve and develop our AI video workflow



## Tools



We use tools such as:



* Higgsfield

* Seedance / Seedance 2.5

* Kling

* AI image-generation tools

* CapCut or similar editing software



**Experience with these tools or similar AI image/video generation platforms is a strong plus.**



Experience creating **AI animation, character-driven videos, cinematic AI videos, short films, or narrative content** is especially valuable.



## What We're Looking For



* Strong visual judgment

* Experience with AI image or video generation

* Ability to keep characters consistent across scenes

* Understanding of prompting and reference-image workflows

* Strong attention to small visual details

* Ability to follow scripts and creative direction closely

* Comfortable generating multiple versions until a scene looks right

* Basic video editing skills

* Creative problem-solving ability



We are specifically looking for someone interested in **AI filmmaking, animation, storytelling, and character-based content**, not someone whose experience is primarily AI UGC avatars or talking-head advertisements.



## How to Apply



Please send:



* A short introduction

* Your portfolio or examples of AI-generated work

* Examples of **story-driven, animated, cinematic, or character-based AI videos** are strongly preferred

* The AI video/image tools you have experience using

title: Construction Estimator / Drawing Reader - US Commercial Projects (Project-Based, Can Become Full-Time)
description:
# Construction Estimator / Drawing Reader - US Commercial Projects (Project-Based, Can Become Full-Time)



**RULE #1: READ THIS ENTIRE POST BEFORE YOU APPLY.** There are three rules in this post. Rule #1 is right here. Rules #2 and #3 are further down. Applications that skip them will be deleted without a reply.



---



## About Us



On Site Contracting is a commercial general contractor in the United States (Ohio, Pennsylvania, West Virginia). We build ground-ups and fit-outs for business owners - franchisees and independent operators. We operate as a "paper GC": we don't self-perform, we coordinate the best subcontractors on every trade. That means accurate takeoffs and fast, clean sub outreach are the backbone of our business.



## What You'll Be Doing



- Read and interpret US commercial construction drawings - architectural, structural, MEP - plus specs and detail sheets

- Do full callouts and takeoffs by trade (demo, framing, drywall, electrical, plumbing, HVAC, flooring, millwork, finishes, fire protection, etc.)

- Build clean scope sheets/bid packages for each trade so subs know exactly what they're pricing

- Contact potential subcontractors, send them the scope and drawings, and chase them until we have real numbers back

- Track incoming bids, level them side by side, and flag gaps, exclusions, and anything missing from the drawings

- Report findings back in a clear, organized format we can price a job from



## Immediate Work



We have **two commercial restaurant remodels inside a strip plaza** that need to be estimated and priced ASAP. This is your first assignment, and it starts this week. Move fast and accurately on these and there is a lot more behind them.



## Requirements

- **Hands-on experience reading drawings for projects located in the United States.** This is non-negotiable. US plan sets, US trade standards, US terminology.

- Proven experience doing callouts/takeoffs and soliciting pricing from subcontractors

- Comfortable
ing and calling US-based subs and following up until you get a number

- Strong written English

- Able to work US Eastern Time hours when needed for sub follow-up

- Bluebeam, PlanSwift, On-Screen Takeoff, or similar - tell us what you use

- Reliable internet and the ability to start immediately



## The Arrangement



- Starts as **project-based** work, beginning with the two restaurant remodels

- Strong performance turns this into a **full-time position within 60-90 days**

- Rate: $5-10 per hour based on experience. Higher end for project-based work; lower end if/when this converts to full-time. First assignment is likely about 20-30 hours this week.



---



## HOW TO APPLY - READ CAREFULLY



There are three rules. All three are mandatory. If you miss any one of them, you will not be considered.



**RULE #1 - Read this entire post from beginning to end before applying.**



**RULE #2 - You must send in a video with your application.** No video, no interview. A phone camera is fine. We are not judging your production quality.



**RULE #3 - In that video, you must do two things:**



1. **State all three rules out loud** - Rule #1, Rule #2, and Rule #3.

2. **Tell us the exact experience and specific projects you have worked on in the United States** that you believe apply to this role and will help us. Name the project types, the trades you took off, the software you used, and what you were responsible for. Be specific. "I have 5 years of estimating experience" tells us nothing.



Keep the video under 5 minutes.



HOW TO SEND THE VIDEO (required):

1. Record on your phone.

2. Upload to Loom, Google Drive (anyone-with-link), or YouTube (unlisted).

3. Paste the full https link in your OnlineJobs application message / cover letter. Do not attach a huge video file. Do not say "I can send the video later." No link = automatic delete.



Example of what to paste:

Video: [paste your Loom or Drive or YouTube unlisted link here]



## Deadline



**All applications must be in by Monday, September 14, 9:00 AM Eastern Time.**



We are interviewing Monday and Tuesday and starting work immediately this week. Do not apply if you cannot start right away.

Please do not send a generic application. I care much more about organization, attention to detail and your thought process than a long résumé.

title: INBOUND APPOINTMENT SETTER — HAIR SALON (WARM FACEBOOK/INSTAGRAM LEADS, $1,250–$2,000/MO OTE + 13TH MONTH PAY)
description:
READ THIS FIRST



We're hiring ONE full-time Inbound Appointment Setter to call warm leads from our
 and Instagram ad campaigns for a color-specialist hair salon in Fontana, California.



This is NOT cold calling. Every lead you speak to has already raised their hand by submitting their info through one of our ads. Your job is to reach them fast, build trust quickly, understand what they actually want, and guide them into a booked appointment.



This role demands two things at once: sharp conversational judgment AND tight process discipline. The conversations are where you win or lose the booking. The process — cadences, call dispositions, CRM hygiene, follow-up tasks — is what makes the whole system work and what lets us measure anything. You need both. People who are great at one and sloppy at the other don't last here.



On the conversation side, what we're really hiring for is the ability to think on your feet. Someone replies three days later with just "sorry, been busy." Someone says they want highlights but describes something else entirely. Someone says "that's a bit far for me" but what they really mean is they don't see why it's worth the drive. If you can read what people actually mean and move the conversation forward without being told what to say next, you'll do well here.



If you need to be spoon-fed a script for every situation, this won't work.



THIS IS A SALES ROLE. YOU NEED AT LEAST 6 MONTHS OF EXPERIENCE

PERSUADING PEOPLE AND MOVING THEM TOWARD A BOOKED APPOINTMENT

OR A SALE.



OTE: $1,250–$2,000/month (base $900–$1,000 + uncapped performance bonuses).

13th month pay included — paid every December, on top of your base. Not baked in. Not restructured. A full extra month of base pay, added on top.



---



ABOUT THE COMPANY



You'll be employed by Midnight Siren, a growth and client acquisition company that operates and supports beauty service businesses. Your day-to-day work focuses on a family-owned, color-specialist hair salon in Fontana, California that has served the Inland Empire for over 21 years.



The salon has 4.9 stars on Google with 200+ reviews and a stylist team with 75+ combined years of experience. The business is real, established, and respected in its market.



You'll work directly under Ethan, the founder of Midnight Siren — no middle managers, no agency layers between you and the person making decisions. The Midnight Siren team is small and tightly focused. The stylists at salon handle the in-salon experience; you and Ethan handle everything that gets a client booked.



A note on team structure: you will be the only appointment setter on the team. Your day-to-day working relationship is directly with Ethan. There are no peer-level coworkers, no team chat with other appointment setters, no group energy to feed off. If you thrive with autonomy, clear systems, and a direct manager relationship, this works well. If you need a team environment or peer social dynamic to stay motivated, this will feel isolating over time.



We're in an active scaling phase. Core processes exist and are being refined. They don't change daily, but they evolve as we learn. If you like improving systems alongside a team, you'll fit. If you want a fully crystallized corporate environment where nothing ever shifts, you won't.



---



WHAT YOU'LL ACTUALLY BE DOING



This is a front-line revenue role, not customer support.



Daily:



- Call new
/Instagram ad leads within minutes of opt-in (speed matters — you'll have task notifications throughout the day)

- Run our call script for the structured parts of the call, and use our frameworks + your own judgment for discovery and objection handling. The script covers the greeting, the offer, pricing, and the booking ask. Discovery can't be fully scripted — clients say what they say, and you'll need to adapt in real time.

- Respond to inbound SMS,
 
, and Instagram DMs that get escalated to a human when our AI can't handle them

- Collect cards on file via secure link (never over the phone), book appointments, reschedule, and cancel

- Call no-shows to get them back on the calendar

- Coordinate with stylists about client requests and scheduling needs

- Create follow-up tasks in HighLevel (our CRM)

- Submit a brief end-of-day report with your numbers



Weekly:



- One coaching/review call with Ethan (~30–45 min)

- Async coaching via Loom video reviews on your live call recordings between meetings

- Review your KPIs, own your numbers, and bring data-backed ideas to improve them



During training (first 2–4 weeks):



We'll meet daily for live coaching to get you fully ramped before transitioning to the weekly + async cadence.



---



A WORD ON THE CALL SCRIPT (READ CAREFULLY)



We use a script. We also need you to think.



Where the script is fixed: the greeting, how we introduce the salon, how we present the offer, how we state pricing, the booking ask, and our core objection responses. These are tested and they work. You run them as written. Your tone, warmth, and pacing are what make them sound human — not changing the words.



Where the script can't help you: everything a real client throws at you. A vague text with no context. A client describing a service using the wrong name. Someone who's hesitant but won't say why. Someone who asks about price before you've figured out what they actually want. There is no script for these. There's a framework, and there's your judgment.



This is the part people underestimate. A big chunk of this job is not reciting — it's listening to what someone actually means and figuring out the next move in seconds, while they're on the phone with you.



Scripts do change here, but only based on data. If you bring an idea for a better line, we'll A/B test it. If it wins, it becomes the script. What we don't do is let setters freelance changes on the fly, because then we can't measure what works.



If you want to be told exactly what to say in every situation, this role will frustrate you. If you like having strong structure AND room to think, you'll do well.



---



SCHEDULE (PACIFIC TIME — GRAVEYARD SHIFT IN PHILIPPINES)



All schedule references in this post are in US Pacific Time. Because PH is 15-16 hours ahead of California, each shift starts late at night your time and ends the following morning.

- US workdays: Monday through Friday

- US days off: Saturday and Sunday

- Hours per day: 8 hours of work + 1 hour of break (30 min lunch + 2× 15 min breaks, or 30 min lunch + 1× 30 min break — your call)

- Pacific Time (US): 7:45 AM – 4:45 PM PST



Philippine Time during US Standard Time (roughly November through mid-March):



Shift runs 11:45 PM – 8:45 AM PHT

- A US Monday shift = late Monday night through Tuesday morning your time

- A US Friday shift = late Friday night through Saturday morning your time

- Your days off in PH local time: Sunday and Monday (until your shift starts late Monday night)



Philippine Time during US Daylight Savings Time (roughly mid-March through early November):



- Shift runs 10:45 PM – 7:45 AM PHT

- Same day-shift logic as above — shift starts the previous calendar evening in PH



This schedule is FIXED. It's based on data showing when our booking demand peaks. If you need flexible hours, rotating shifts, or plan to hold another job during these times, this role is not a fit.

Please re-read this section carefully and make sure BOTH the standard-time and daylight-savings schedules work for you long-term before applying. The 1-hour shift twice a year is non-negotiable — it follows US business hours. Please make sure BOTH schedules work for you long-term before applying.



If you have never worked a graveyard shift before, think carefully before applying. We will ask you specifically how you plan to structure your sleep, and how you'll make the schedule work alongside your family or partner. "I'll figure it out" is not an answer that gets you hired. This shift is sustainable for people who plan for it and difficult for people who don't.



---



COMPENSATION



Base pay:



$900–$1,000/month (depending on experience), paid via Wise on the 1st and 15th of every month.



13TH MONTH PAY included — paid every December on top of your regular base, not restructured into it. Prorated in your first year if you start mid-year. Total annualized base compensation including 13th month: $11,700–$13,000.



Performance bonuses (uncapped, paid monthly):



- $3 per new client showed appointment

- $2 per existing client showed appointment

- $1 per rebooking confirmation (low-effort confirmation calls for clients who already booked through the salon)



Tiered cumulative threshold bonuses (paid monthly):



- +$75 at 90 showed appointments/month

- +$150 at 120 showed appointments/month

- +$350 at 150 showed appointments/month



Worked examples:



Baseline performer — 90 showed appointments/month:

- Base: $950 (midpoint)

- Performance: ~$225 (avg $2.50/show × 90)

- Threshold bonus: $75

- Total: ~$1,250/month



Solid performer — 120 showed appointments/month:

- Base: $950

- Performance: ~$300 (avg $2.50/show × 120)

- Threshold bonus: $225 ($75 + $150)

- Total: ~$1,475/month



Top performer — 150 showed appointments/month (90% show rate on ~167 booked):

- Base: $1,000

- Performance: $450 ($3×90 new + $2×20 existing + $1×40 rebooking)

- Threshold bonuses: $575 ($75 + $150 + $350)

- Total: ~$2,025/month



This is a PERFORMANCE-PAY ROLE. 30–50% of your monthly income should be earned through bonuses. The base is intentionally modest. If you want a high guaranteed salary with low expectations, this is not the role.



---



OTHER BENEFITS



1. Annual performance-based raise after your first year

2. 14 days of PTO per year, single bucket, available after 90-day probation (use for vacation, holidays, sickness — your call). For planned multi-day time off, give us at least 1 week's notice so we can plan coverage. Emergencies are understood — just communicate as soon as you can.

3. 90-day initial probation period. Pay is NOT REDUCED during probation.



To confirm you have read this post in full, include the word BURGUNDY in your answer to the final question on the application form



---



TARGET KPIs



- Lead to Booking Rate: 25%+

- Show Rate: 90%+

- Bookings per day: 4–9

- Showed appointments per month: 100–160

- Daily volume: Finish all assigned tasks each day. We supply ~17–25 leads per day plus follow-ups, no-shows, reactivations, and rebooking confirmations. HIGH CALL VOLUME (150–250 CALLS/DAY) IS NORMAL AND NON-NEGOTIABLE. If that sounds overwhelming instead of energizing, this is not a fit.



---



WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR



Background:



- Female candidates tend to perform best with our 35–65 female clientele, so we especially encourage strong female applicants — but the role is open to all genders.

- Bilingual (English + Spanish) is a plus but not required.



Non-negotiable skills:



The five that matter most — these are what we screen hardest for:



- Real-time thinking. You generate a good response in seconds, not minutes. Under pressure, with no script in front of you. This is the single biggest predictor of success in this role.

- Inferential listening. You hear what someone means, not just what they said. A client says "I need to talk to my husband first" — she's usually not asking for permission, she's telling you something about price or certainty that she doesn't want to say directly. If you take everything at face value, you'll lose bookings.

- Conversational initiative. You never dead-end a conversation, and you don't give up on a lead that's still alive. A client says "that's kind of far for me" — a weak setter says "no problem, thanks anyway" and loses her. What she's actually telling you is that she doesn't believe the drive is worth it yet. That's not a rejection, it's an assumption you haven't disproven. Answering someone's question is only half a response; the other half is the move that keeps things going.

- Rapport building. You can get someone to open up and feel comfortable with you fast. This is the biggest factor in whether someone books. These are emotional decisions, not logical ones. You don't need American cultural references — you need to make people feel heard, understood, and safe.

- Diagnostic reframing. You can say someone's problem back to them more clearly than they said it. When you do that, people assume you have the solution. It's the fastest way to build trust that exists.



Everything else:



- ADVANCED ENGLISH WITH MINIMAL ACCENT. An American listener should not need to strain to understand you. If we have to focus to follow what you're saying, that's a disqualifier.

- STRONG SPOKEN COMMUNICATION — CLEAR, CONFIDENT VOICE. YOU DO NOT RAMBLE. YOU ARE NOT SOFT-SPOKEN. If you fill silence with words because dead air makes you nervous, this won't work.

- Typing speed: 40 wpm minimum (60+ strongly preferred). You'll be taking notes and sending texts while talking. You'll submit a typing test screenshot with your application.

- Process discipline. Every call gets dispositioned correctly. Every lead moves through the right cadence. Every opportunity gets marked accurately in the CRM. This isn't optional admin — it's how we measure everything. Great conversations with sloppy process still means we're flying blind.

- Script discipline for the structured parts of the call.

- Natural call control. You can guide a conversation efficiently without talking over clients or letting calls drift. You redirect politely and keep the call outcome-focused.

- Sales experience: 6 months minimum (1 year+ preferred). Job-hopping resumes (multiple roles under 3–6 months each) will be disqualified.

- Comfortable holding the line on policies (rescheduling, deposits, etc.) without weakening the script or over-promising.

- Objection handling — you acknowledge, ask questions to reframe, and guide the client. You don't fire off rebuttals that invoke more resistance.

- CRM literacy. GoHighLevel experience strongly preferred.

- High data accuracy. You enter info correctly the first time. This is a precision role, not a speed-only one.

- Strong working memory and multitasking — you can listen, think, type, recall rules, and follow scripts simultaneously without freezing.

- Emotional steadiness under high-volume periods. Spikes happen. You execute calm under load.



Preferred:



- Familiarity with the salon/beauty industry

- Personal interest in beauty or self-care

- Experience working with older female clientele (35–65)

- Experience with Slack, Slite, Airtable, Claude or ChatGPT (we use AI to streamline daily work — if you can leverage it, you'll move faster)



Mindset (MOST IMPORTANT):



We'd rather hire someone who's a 10 in mindset and 7 in sales skill than the reverse. Here's what we mean:



- Ownership & volume mindset — you take responsibility for outcomes, not tasks. You see high-volume, repetitive work as leverage, not burnout.

- Process discipline — you operate consistently inside defined systems. You let your personality show through tone and warmth, not by changing the words.

- Sales psychology — you understand how to influence through trust, value framing, and subtle urgency. You communicate with intention, not chit-chat.

- Speed bias — you move fast, close loops quickly, and accelerate under pressure instead of slowing down.

- Coachability — you receive feedback without ego and adapt immediately. No defensiveness, no excuses.

- KPI awareness — you understand the numbers behind your role and how your daily actions move them.



---



TECH REQUIREMENTS



Non-negotiable:



- Internet minimum requirements: 50 Mbps download, 10 Mbps upload, ping under 80ms. Stable connection. We will test your speed and audio live from your actual work setup before we hire.

- Backup plan for outages. If your internet or power cuts out mid-shift, you need a real fallback — mobile hotspot, secondary ISP, UPS, co-working space, or some combination. You'll describe your specific backup setup in your application.

- Computer: 8 GB RAM minimum (16+ preferred). Processor: Intel Core i5 or equivalent, 8th generation or newer. SSD preferred. Working laptop or desktop

- Mouse

- Wired headset with boom mic (3.5mm or USB-C). No Bluetooth, no laptop mic, no AirPods.

- Webcam — laptop built-in is fine. You'll be on camera for interviews, training, and coaching calls.

- Quiet, dedicated workspace. No roosters, no karaoke neighbors, no babies crying, no traffic, no dogs barking during calls. We will hear it on the call, and so will our clients.



Preferred:



- Second monitor

- You already own a headset that meets the requirements above (we'll provide one if you don't, but having your own helps you start faster)



---



DO NOT APPLY IF:



- You struggle to think quickly and respond in real time. If you need a moment to figure out what to say, this role will be painful. Clients don't wait.

- You need the client to lead the conversation. If you're comfortable answering questions but not steering, this isn't it.

- You can't hold a conversation without a script telling you what to say next.

- You type slowly. Under 40 wpm means you'll fall behind on notes and texts while you're talking.

- You have less than 6 months of experience persuading people, handling objections, and closing toward a booked appointment or sale.

- Your spoken English is hard to understand on the phone — this is a phone role first and the single biggest dealbreaker

- You're juggling multiple clients or planning to freelance on the side. THIS MUST BE YOUR ONLY JOB. We track performance closely and will discover this fast.

- You want a high guaranteed salary with low performance pressure

- You don't like high call volume or you find scripts "suffocating"

- You see remote work as "work whenever you feel like it"

- You can't sustain a graveyard shift long-term

- You're looking for a short-term gig — we expect a minimum 12-month commitment after probation



---



HIRING PROCESS



1. Application via Tally form (link below) — includes voice recording, Loom video, internet speed screenshot, backup plan description, and a few short written questions

2. 15-minute pre-screen async interview

3. First-round interview with Ethan (~45 min) — includes live roleplay

4. Second-round interview with Ethan (~45 min) — final fit + offer discussion

5. Offer

6. Paid training begins immediately after offer acceptance



A NOTE ON TIMING



We hire for this role on a rolling basis and are always reviewing applications, so the timeline varies. Sometimes we're interviewing within a week of your application. Sometimes a seat opens a month or two later. If you're a strong fit, we'll keep you in our pipeline and reach out when there's an opening.



---



HOW TO APPLY



Submit your application through this Tally form: | 
 |



IMPORTANT: There is a confirmation requirement embedded in this post. Applications that miss it will be skipped regardless of experience.



The form will ask for:



- A screenshot of your typing test results (
)

- A screenshot of your internet speedtest (speedtest.net)

- A screenshot of your computer specs (RAM and processor)

- A description of your backup plan for power/internet outages

- A few short questions to gauge fit

- A short voice recording (Vocaroo or similar)

- A short Loom video introducing yourself



Applications submitted via direct messages on OnlineJobs.ph will NOT be reviewed. Use the Tally form.



---



Looking forward to meeting the right person.



Ethan

Founder, Midnight Siren



---



Full-Time | Long-Term | Remote | Pacific Time (Graveyard Shift in PH)

- Diagnostic reframing. You can say someone's problem back to them more clearly than they said it. When you do that, people assume you have the solution. It's the fastest way to build trust that exists.



Everything else:



- ADVANCED ENGLISH WITH MINIMAL ACCENT. An American listener should not need to strain to understand you. If we have to focus to follow what you're saying, that's a disqualifier.

- STRONG SPOKEN COMMUNICATION — CLEAR, CONFIDENT VOICE. YOU DO NOT RAMBLE. YOU ARE NOT SOFT-SPOKEN. If you fill silence with words because dead air makes you nervous, this won't work.

- Typing speed: 40 wpm minimum (60+ strongly preferred). You'll be taking notes and sending texts while talking. You'll submit a typing test screenshot with your application.

- Process discipline. Every call gets dispositioned correctly. Every lead moves through the right cadence. Every opportunity gets marked accurately in the CRM. This isn't optional admin — it's how we measure everything. Great conversations with sloppy process still means we're flying blind.

- Script discipline for the structured parts of the call.

- Natural call control. You can guide a conversation efficiently without talking over clients or letting calls drift. You redirect politely and keep the call outcome-focused.

- Sales experience: 6 months minimum (1 year+ preferred). Job-hopping resumes (multiple roles under 3–6 months each) will be disqualified.

- Comfortable holding the line on policies (rescheduling, deposits, etc.) without weakening the script or over-promising.

- Objection handling — you acknowledge, ask questions to reframe, and guide the client. You don't fire off rebuttals that invoke more resistance.

- CRM literacy. GoHighLevel experience strongly preferred.

- High data accuracy. You enter info correctly the first time. This is a precision role, not a speed-only one.

- Strong working memory and multitasking — you can listen, think, type, recall rules, and follow scripts simultaneously without freezing.

- Emotional steadiness under high-volume periods. Spikes happen. You execute calm under load.



Preferred:



- Familiarity with the salon/beauty industry

- Personal interest in beauty or self-care

- Experience working with older female clientele (35–65)

- Experience with Slack, Slite, Airtable, Claude or ChatGPT (we use AI to streamline daily work — if you can leverage it, you'll move faster)



Mindset (MOST IMPORTANT):



We'd rather hire someone who's a 10 in mindset and 7 in sales skill than the reverse. Here's what we mean:



- Ownership & volume mindset — you take responsibility for outcomes, not tasks. You see high-volume, repetitive work as leverage, not burnout.

- Process discipline — you operate consistently inside defined systems. You let your personality show through tone and warmth, not by changing the words.

- Sales psychology — you understand how to influence through trust, value framing, and subtle urgency. You communicate with intention, not chit-chat.

- Speed bias — you move fast, close loops quickly, and accelerate under pressure instead of slowing down.

- Coachability — you receive feedback without ego and adapt immediately. No defensiveness, no excuses.

- KPI awareness — you understand the numbers behind your role and how your daily actions move them.



---



TECH REQUIREMENTS



Non-negotiable:



- Internet minimum requirements: 50 Mbps download, 10 Mbps upload, ping under 80ms. Stable connection. We will test your speed and audio live from your actual work setup before we hire.

- Backup plan for outages. If your internet or power cuts out mid-shift, you need a real fallback — mobile hotspot, secondary ISP, UPS, co-working space, or some combination. You'll describe your specific backup setup in your application.

- Computer: 8 GB RAM minimum (16+ preferred). Processor: Intel Core i5 or equivalent, 8th generation or newer. SSD preferred. Working laptop or desktop

- Mouse

- Wired headset with boom mic (3.5mm or USB-C). No Bluetooth, no laptop mic, no AirPods.

- Webcam — laptop built-in is fine. You'll be on camera for interviews, training, and coaching calls.

- Quiet, dedicated workspace. No roosters, no karaoke neighbors, no babies crying, no traffic, no dogs barking during calls. We will hear it on the call, and so will our clients.



Preferred:



- Second monitor

- You already own a headset that meets the requirements above (we'll provide one if you don't, but having your own helps you start faster)



---



DO NOT APPLY IF:



- You struggle to think quickly and respond in real time. If you need a moment to figure out what to say, this role will be painful. Clients don't wait.

- You need the client to lead the conversation. If you're comfortable answering questions but not steering, this isn't it.

- You can't hold a conversation without a script telling you what to say next.

- You type slowly. Under 40 wpm means you'll fall behind on notes and texts while you're talking.

- You have less than 6 months of experience persuading people, handling objections, and closing toward a booked appointment or sale.

- Your spoken English is hard to understand on the phone — this is a phone role first and the single biggest dealbreaker

- You're juggling multiple clients or planning to freelance on the side. THIS MUST BE YOUR ONLY JOB. We track performance closely and will discover this fast.

- You want a high guaranteed salary with low performance pressure

- You don't like high call volume or you find scripts "suffocating"

- You see remote work as "work whenever you feel like it"

- You can't sustain a graveyard shift long-term

- You're looking for a short-term gig — we expect a minimum 12-month commitment after probation



---



HIRING PROCESS



1. Application via Tally form (link below) — includes voice recording, Loom video, internet speed screenshot, backup plan description, and a few short written questions

2. 15-minute pre-screen async interview

3. First-round interview with Ethan (~45 min) — includes live roleplay

4. Second-round interview with Ethan (~45 min) — final fit + offer discussion

5. Offer

6. Paid training begins immediately after offer acceptance



A NOTE ON TIMING



We hire for this role on a rolling basis and are always reviewing applications, so the timeline varies. Sometimes we're interviewing within a week of your application. Sometimes a seat opens a month or two later. If you're a strong fit, we'll keep you in our pipeline and reach out when there's an opening.



---



HOW TO APPLY



Submit your application through this Tally form: |

IMPORTANT: There is a confirmation requirement embedded in this post. Applications that miss it will be skipped regardless of experience.



The form will ask for:

)

- A description of your backup plan for power/internet outages

Applications submitted via direct messages on OnlineJobs.ph will NOT be reviewed. Use the Tally form.

Looking forward to meeting the right person.



Ethan

title: Virtual Assistant (Remote)
description:
Kolbe 15 is a founder community built around real, in-person connection, peer groups, curated experiences, retreats, and public events for ambitious founders and operators. We're looking for a Virtual Assistant who can own both the research and the execution side of running it, so the founder can stay focused on members, partnerships, and content instead of logistics.



The Role



This isn't a "do exactly what I say" assistant role. If we're planning a trip to Mexico and you're told "we need A, B, C," you research the options, find the most suitable price, negotiate with vendors, and bring back a decision-ready recommendation, not just a list of links. That's the standard for everything below.



What You'll Do



- Trip & event planning — research venues, activities, and vendors for retreats and events (e.g. the Tulum trip); find the best options, negotiate pricing, and manage bookings

- Grants — search for relevant grants, determine eligibility, and apply on Kolbe's behalf

- Sponsorship & partnerships — find and reach out to potential sponsors and resources, track the pipeline, and keep relationships moving

- Calendar management — keep the founder's calendar accurate and up to date; schedule meetings and events

- Event coordination & member communication — manage logistics for recurring activities (Tuesday Runs, cohort weekends, panel series) and communicate directly with members and attendees

- Speaker/panelist coordination — outreach, prep materials, and logistics for event speakers and panelists

- Outreach tracking — keep the outreach log and member/founder directory current so nothing falls through

- Inbox triage— flag what needs a personal reply vs. what you can handle directly

- Light expense/invoice tracking

- Represent Kolbe 15 professionally — including keeping a polished, professional LinkedIn presence for outward-facing communication



What We're Looking For



- Strong research instincts — you dig past the first search result and bring back a real recommendation, not just raw options

- Comfortable negotiating with vendors and external parties on Kolbe's behalf

- Takes initiative rather than waiting for every step to be spelled out

- Highly organized — can juggle multiple live projects (a trip, a grant application, a sponsor pipeline) at once

- Excellent written communication — comfortable reaching out to new people and representing the community well

- Professional, presentable LinkedIn profile

- Comfortable with Google Workspace, Luma, and picking up new tools as needed

- Trustworthy with sensitive information (applicant data, member details, finances)



How to Apply



Along with your resume/LinkedIn, complete the following exercise. This isn't about a "correct" answer — it's about how you think when you don't have much to go on, since that's exactly day one of this role.



**All you're given to start:** the founder's name is Behzad Hariri, based in Toronto, Canada. That's it.



1. Research who he is and what he does, using whatever's publicly available.

2. Based on what you find, plan out a full day for him — that would actually be useful and interesting to *him specifically*, not a generic "productive day" template.

3. Write up your reasoning: what you found, what you inferred, what assumptions you made, and what you'd ask him directly if you could.



Excited to see what you come up with

 & General Administration

s

Insurance

Annual Administration

Who We're Looking For
